conclusions.statement: Score translation accuracy with multi-reference semantic cosine as a SCREEN, not a verdict — reserve a blind LLM/SME judge for the ambiguous tail.
conclusions.detail: Single-reference string/cosine breaks on valid Korean synonyms; multi-ref (all KR synonyms) chrF + max BGE cosine fixes that. But even multi-ref understates valid-but-divergent translations: it rated organism context +2.8 chrF while a blind judge preferred it 69% vs 31%.
conclusions.author: research-agent

conclusions.statement: Back-translation LINKS Korean terms to the right SNOMED concept ~63-68%@1 at full scale, but is a poor ERROR detector — the round-trip LLM normalises errors away.
conclusions.detail: Full 36k extension: recall@1 63% (hybrid) / 68% (dense). As an MT error detector AUC ~0.5: recovery is identical for correct and incorrect candidates.
conclusions.author: research-agent

conclusions.statement: A non-generative direct cross-lingual check beats back-translation for error detection (AUC 0.58-0.62 vs 0.51), but only a Korean reference gives a strong (0.98) check.
conclusions.detail: Skipping the laundering LLM recovers error signal; absolute strength is still weak reference-free (BGE compresses cross-lingual cosine). Strong detection needs a Korean reference -> multi-reference semantic validation where references exist.
conclusions.author: research-agent

conclusions.statement: SNOMED parent context improves EN->KO translation on the AMBIGUOUS tail (judge ~2:1 on organisms / qualifier values) but hurts concrete types — add it conditionally, fenced.
conclusions.detail: Neutral on the mean (harsh metric), but a blind judge shows organism 69% / qualifier 66% wins and body-structure/disorder losses. Naive '(tag)' formatting leaks into output; fence the context.
conclusions.author: research-agent

conclusions.statement: Claude Fable 5 works as GEPA's feedback-judge: from a one-line seed it drove GEPA to a KO translation prompt scoring 55.6% exact / 81.6 chrF on the held-out test — beating both Opus-induced guides but not the hand guide v5_1 (58.1% / 84.1).
conclusions.detail:
Setup (investigation fable_gepa_judge_v1): GEPA optimised a translation prompt seeded from ko_minimal_seed (a single instruction line). Task + reflection LM = gemma4-26b-qat (served vLLM). Reward = BGE-M3 semantic cosine to the gold Korean (exact->1.0), a local/free dense signal. Claude Fable 5 supplied ONLY the sparse reflective feedback GEPA learns from — gated to genuine reflection, score<0.9, capped at 40 calls, cached.

GEPA run (job b7647eeaca10, auto=light, 396s): on GEPA's own dev-50 metric the seed improved 28.0%->42.0% exact (mean semantic 0.472->0.567, chrF 66.3->71.3). Fable fired only 10 judge calls. The evolved guide induced structured, transferable rules purely from Fable's critiques: preserve procedural head nouns (초음파검사/촬영 vs bare 초음파), anatomical precision (장딴지 over obscure 비복부), classifier-omission exceptions, and one-to-one back-mapping to prevent semantic collapse.

Held-out test (job 22c4b89b2ef3, kr_test_split=124, SAME eval infra as the baselines — gemma4-26b-qat + pooled_legacy exemplars): 55.6% exact / 81.6 chrF / 0.742 composite. Baselines on test: hand v5_1 58.1%/84.1; ko_induced_guide 50.0%/80.7; ko_induced_v1 50.8%/80.0.

Read: Fable's judgment ALONE lifted a trivial one-line seed to near-expert quality (within 2.5 pts exact / 2.5 chrF of a human-tuned guide) and clearly surpassed both prior automated (Opus-induced) guides — a strong positive signal for Fable-as-GEPA-judge. It did not beat the hand guide. Caveats: single run / single seed / auto=light budget; dspy_splits are procedure-only; a larger GEPA budget or more Fable calls (10 of 40 used) may close the remaining gap.

conclusions.statement: CORRECTS conclusion-5. Fable works as a GEPA feedback-judge — evidenced by a CLEAN 28%->42% dev-exact lift from a one-line seed — but the held-out TEST comparison (GEPA 55.6% vs hand v5_1 58.1%) is invalidated as a quality measure by ~88% gold-in-exemplar leakage.
conclusions.detail:
The dspy_splits are Korean SNOMED extension procedure concepts, and the pooled_legacy exemplar corpus contains that same extension (39k SNOMED + 18k synonym pairs). So for 87.9% of test terms (109/124) the exact gold Korean was among the retrieved exemplars fed to the model (verified in the eval's own exemplar cache lookup_cache.exemplars_pooled_legacy_ko_1aca69d6.json). The test numbers therefore measure exemplar-selection, not from-scratch translation, and are inflated — this affects GEPA+Fable (55.6%), hand v5_1 (58.1%) and the Opus-induced guides (~50%) equally.

What survives: the GEPA run (job b7647eeaca10) and its internal dev-50 metric used a DIFFERENT cache (data/sme_review/2026-04-24/lookup_cache.json) with 0% gold leak, and the DSPy translator returns NO exemplars on a cache miss (_format_exemplars). So the seed->evolved improvement 28.0%->42.0% exact on held-out dev is CLEAN and is the trustworthy evidence that Fable's feedback genuinely improves translation from a one-line seed. Caveat: train/eval regime mismatch — GEPA optimised gold-free, the final test eval was gold-leaked.

Action needed for a valid cross-guide test comparison: (a) add self-concept exclusion at exemplar retrieval (lookup_pairs has none), or (b) re-evaluate on the ~100 SME-authored terms that are NOT in the Korean extension (hence not in the exemplar pool). Supersede conclusion-5 with this once confirmed.

conclusions.statement: LEAKAGE-FREE verdict (supersedes conclusion-6): with the query concept's own canonical SNOMED entries excluded from the exemplars, the hand guide v5_1 (36.3% exact / 70.1 chrF) clearly beats the GEPA(Fable) guide (21.8% / 63.9) on kr_test_split. Leakage had inflated both by ~20 exact points and hidden a 14.5-point gap behind an apparent 2.5-point one.
conclusions.detail:
After rebuilding the exemplar pool with per-row sctid + provenance and adding sctid self-exclusion to retrieval (the query concept's FSN + synonyms are dropped, other-vocabulary translations kept and shown WITH provenance), two clean held-out evals on kr_test_split (124), same model/pool/exclusion-cache:
- hand v5_1: 36.3% exact / 70.1 chrF (run 6646ab05591c)
- GEPA(Fable) guide: 21.8% exact / 63.9 chrF (run df42e169939c)
Exclusion audit (identical for both, from the shared cache): 270 exemplars dropped across 111/124 queries; gold removed for 108 (=87%, confirming the measured leak); residual gold via another source = 0 (no EDI/KCD7 duplicate leaked it). Compare the LEAKY numbers (v5_1 58.1%, GEPA 55.6%): leakage inflated both ~+20 exact points and compressed the gap.

Interpretation: (1) The leaky test comparison was meaningless as a quality measure; the clean one shows the hand guide is substantially better than the Fable-GEPA guide as it stands. (2) IMPORTANT FAIRNESS CAVEAT: the GEPA guide was OPTIMISED in a different regime (its DSPy translator used the sme_review cache, which returns NO exemplars on a miss — near-exemplar-free), then evaluated here with pooled-but-self-excluded exemplars + provenance. That train/eval mismatch likely handicaps it. A fair verdict on Fable-as-GEPA-judge needs a GEPA RE-OPTIMISATION in this same clean pooled-excluded regime (deferred, D3). So this establishes the leakage-corrected BASELINE comparison, not a final verdict on the method. (3) The methodological win stands: Fable's feedback did drive a real clean dev improvement (28->42% on GEPA's gold-free dev metric, run b7647eeaca10).

conclusions.statement: Exact-match understates EN→KO translation quality by ~18% of items; embeddings gauge closeness only with a Korean reference (KO↔KO), not reference-free EN↔KO.
conclusions.detail: On 3,693 procedure/therapy forward candidates (BGE-M3): of the 1,102 non-exact-match items, 59.6% are semantically equivalent valid synonyms (KO↔KO cosine ≥ τ=0.784; 41% even at τ=0.85), i.e. 17.8% of ALL items that exact-match wrongly zeroes — driven by Sino-Korean/native/loanword variation (칼륨/포타슘, 나트륨/소듐, 세침/가는 바늘). chrF partially credits them but still averages only 0.548, and misses 9.6% entirely (chrF<0.3). The user's reference-free EN↔KO direct comparison is weak (AUC 0.604; rank-normalisation does not help, 0.580) because BGE-M3 compresses cross-lingual pairs (exact-anchor sim_en 0.583 vs non-exact 0.557). Actionable: add a KO↔KO semantic partial-credit scorer to the eval recipe. Caveats: 'valid' is grounded by the embedding threshold itself (not SME-confirmed — validate against task-24 SME ratings); procedure/therapy hierarchy only; script-derived (scripts/analysis/graded_xlingual_closeness.py), not yet a tracked flow.

conclusions.statement: The LLM judge and the Korean SME systematically diverge on register: the judge rewards Sino-Korean/clinical-fluent forms while the SME prefers native-Korean for limbs, surface anatomy, and laterality — so optimizing to the judge drifts away from the human and the judge cannot see it.
conclusions.detail: Concrete demonstration (n=100, batch-1, in-sample): a guide authored by Opus purely from the SME feedback but told to abstract (no examples) defaulted to Sino-Korean anatomy/laterality (경비골, 상완골, 종골, 좌측/우측, 고관절, 조영증강) — exactly the forms the SME corrected AWAY from toward native (정강뼈/종아리뼈, 위팔뼈, 발꿈치뼈, 왼쪽/오른쪽, 엉덩관절, 조영제 사용). The calibrated judge scored this drifted guide HIGHEST (0.936 mean, 96% predicted-accept) while it was FARTHEST from the SME gold (BGE semantic 0.828 vs 0.89-0.91 for the register-aware guides). An LLM author + LLM judge form a closed loop that agrees with itself and drifts from the human. Implication: the calibrated judge (AUC 0.80 vs SME) is usable as an adequacy screen and blind-spot detector but must never be the sole optimization target; the human register preference must be carried as data (explicit rules / a native-vs-Sino lexicon), and the SME corpus stays the anchor.

conclusions.statement: The SME register preference is recoverable as a general directional rule, not an example-bound one: instructing the guide author to state the DIRECTION of the reviewer's edits (Sino->native for limbs/surface, native laterality) recovered the human-alignment lost by naive abstraction, using zero example pairs.
conclusions.detail: Re-running the Opus guide induction with a directional-extraction instruction (still no specific SME term or translation copied) lifted BGE semantic-to-SME-gold from 0.828 to 0.892 overall and 0.812 to 0.896 on the corrected rows, matching the hand-written register-aware guide (v5.2), while the judge score stayed high (0.921). This corrects an earlier overstatement that the register preference 'only lives in the instances' — it is a systematic pattern statable as a rule. Practical consequence: an LLM will silently default to Sino-Korean unless the native-preference direction is pinned explicitly; pin it (rule or lexicon), do not rely on the model abstracting it.

conclusions.statement: A deterministic phonetic-echo detector flags transliteration slips at 100% precision on the SME-100 and a 0.07% flag rate on the 5.8k frontier pool.
conclusions.detail: transliteration_detect romanizes the hangul, reduces romanized-KO and the English to consonant skeletons, and flags high phonetic echo (>=0.70). On the 100 batch-1 SME labels it flags exactly 1 row (Herniogram -> 허니오그램), the known transliteration WRONG, at 100% precision (run 96d5fbaba78d). On the full ~5.8k untranslated pool it flags 4/5796 (0.069%): 3 genuine slips (Herniogram, Molegraphy, Pouchogram) + 1 benign eponym (Laser Doppler -> 레이저 도플러, correctly transliterated) (run 69db8c1acb10). Echo alone separates cleanly (pure transliterations >=0.73; next non-transliteration ~0.61); the register-oracle coverage gate is an optional refinement, off by default because loan fragments (그램 from 밀리그램) leak in. A high-recall, tiny-burden review-triage flag for a failure class similarity is blind to.

conclusions.statement: An LLM acceptability judge catches BOTH SME-confirmed WRONG translations — including the semantic substitution embeddings miss — with the local gemma model matching Sonnet on catch-rate at zero API cost, though Sonnet is better SME-calibrated.
conclusions.detail: acceptability_judge labels each EN->KO pair ACCEPTABLE/PARTIAL/WRONG vs the sme_acceptability_judge_v1 rubric. Over all 100 batch-1 SME labels: gemma4-26b (local vLLM) A/P/W=55/37/8, 3-way 56% / binary 62%, caught 2/2 WRONG (run 4c8e51d5fd8f); Sonnet (Agent SDK) A/P/W=42/52/6, 3-way 65% / binary 69%, caught 2/2 WRONG (run e22a7ced11cf). Both catch the mammogram->'증상치료' (symptom TREATMENT) semantic substitution that cross-lingual similarity ranks mid-pack. Sonnet's label distribution nearly matches the SME's own (47/51/2) so it is better calibrated; gemma is more polarized (more lenient on ACCEPTABLE, harsher on WRONG) but still catches the critical errors — a viable local zero-cost gate. Note the Sonnet arm spawns a bundled Claude CLI subprocess per call (heavy per-item overhead vs the local HTTP path).

conclusions.statement: Similarity-based confidence is blind to both SME-confirmed long-tail error classes; targeted class-specific detectors (a transliteration rule + an LLM judge) are the required complement, not a single similarity gate.
conclusions.detail: The two outright-WRONG translations in batch-1 are both invisible to cross-lingual embedding / back-translation confidence. Transliteration slips (Herniogram) even score in the TOP quintile of cross-lingual similarity because a phonetic echo embeds near its English source; semantic substitutions (mammogram->treatment) rank mid-pack and are drowned out. Reproduced on the SME batch (Spearman(BGE-M3 cosine, SME rating) ~ +0.11, n.s.; mean cosine ~equal across ACCEPTABLE/PARTIAL/WRONG), consistent with the independent snomed_direct_xlingual_verify_v1 result (bad-translation detection AUC ~0.5). The two new detectors close exactly these gaps and should feed the triage layer as per-term features.

conclusions.statement: A same-model Gemma judge→correction loop is not a safe improvement strategy for SME concepts: it makes outputs look better to Gemma while worsening agreement with held-out SME translations.
conclusions.detail: The tracked correction run used the union of the deterministic transliteration flag and Gemma acceptability rejection as triggers, then used Gemma again to revise and re-judge. The post-correction judge distribution improved sharply, but held-out SME exact and chrF moved in the wrong direction. The transliteration rule was precise and removed its flagged case; the harm came from broad judge-triggered rewriting. Future correction should isolate the transliteration-only arm, require an independent correction/judge model, or use a conservative threshold with regression checks.

evidence.label: [local Gemma metric-triggered correction on SME batch 1]

conclusions.statement: Use the stricter balanced candidate for SME batch 2: it combines broad imaging-procedure coverage with targeted likely failures while avoiding batch-1 concepts and close wording variants.
conclusions.detail: Three tracked candidate runs compared coverage-only, active-risk-only, and balanced selection. Coverage-only is broad but contains fewer locally suspected errors; active-only is information-rich but over-concentrates long radiography and other-modality terms. The stricter balanced design retains equal active and coverage arms, spans all major imaging modality groups and term-complexity bins, and excludes prior concepts plus near-template repeats. The packaged CSV includes accept/edit/reject, corrected Korean, error category, and notes fields. Keep task-30 active until the packet is dispatched and the pending taxonomy/consistency features can be folded into a future revision.

conclusions.statement: Full-frontier Gemma self-evaluation indicates a usable baseline but not a release-quality endpoint: most imaging-procedure translations pass, while the partial bucket is the principal remaining correction target and outright wrong outputs form a smaller tail.
conclusions.detail: The complete tracked flow translated every frontier term, applied deterministic transliteration detection, and judged every result with the same local Gemma procedure. Transliteration alerts were uncommon and mostly exposed obvious loanword or untranslated technical-name echoes, so that rule is a focused signal rather than a broad quality screen. Runtime instrumentation also shows that full LLM judging dominates the cost of this workflow. Because prior SME work demonstrated same-model register blind spots, this result should be read as Gemma self-consistency over the frontier, not human acceptance; use the partial/wrong and transliteration subsets to prioritize independent review.

evidence.label: [complete frontier translation, transliteration, and same-Gemma judge]

conclusions.statement: Batched LLM judging is model-dependent and should be calibrated against singleton judgments before operational use.
conclusions.detail: The Gemma sweep shows a systematic leniency shift as batch size increases. Sonnet at batch size ten preserves the overall label distribution more closely, but its term-level agreement remains below the threshold for treating batched and singleton labels as interchangeable. Use Sonnet batching for population-level measurement and candidate triage, retain singleton or SME review for final term-level decisions, and monitor parse coverage and retry overhead on every run.

conclusions.statement: Use the diversity-capped, freshly Gemma-translated packet for Korean SME batch 2 instead of the earlier risk-concentrated candidate.
conclusions.detail: The revised selection preserves equal active-risk and coverage arms while preventing a feedback-associated anatomy or procedure template from dominating. It excludes all batch-1 concepts and stricter near-variants, balances modality and term complexity, freshly translates the selected concepts under the current Korean guide, and emits a single blind reviewer packet. Automated judge and transliteration outputs are retained separately for later calibration, not shown to the SME.

conclusions.statement: Full-frontier Gemma self-evaluation provides a reproducible measure of model self-consistency and review workload, but does not establish translation quality or release readiness.
conclusions.detail: The complete tracked flow translated and judged the frontier with the same local Gemma procedure. Its accept/partial/wrong buckets are useful for measuring that model's self-consistency and prioritising independent review, but they are not estimates of SME acceptance because the judge shares the translator's blind spots. Runtime instrumentation shows that LLM judging dominates the measured workflow cost. Transliteration counts from this run should be treated only as outputs of the current unvalidated rule, not as prevalence or recall estimates.

conclusions.statement: KO↔KO semantic similarity is a strong graded reference-based quality signal, but the earlier ~18% exact-match penalty is a heuristic estimate rather than an SME-validated acceptable-synonym rate.
conclusions.detail: A tracked reproduction over 3,693 procedure/therapy candidates yields the same 17.8% of all items above the old KO↔KO threshold among non-exact matches. Independent calibration on SME-100 shows KO↔KO similarity ranks acceptability strongly (AUC 0.902), but threshold 0.784 is far too permissive as a hard verdict (54% accuracy; 17% specificity). Reference-free EN↔KO remains weak (AUC 0.605; rank-normalised 0.582). Therefore report semantic similarity as graded partial credit and use SME-calibrated review policies; do not relabel the 17.8% as definitively valid translations.

conclusions.statement: Batch-1 SME evidence does not support a systematic Sonnet-versus-SME divergence on Korean register; most apparent register examples are anatomical-scope corrections, and Sonnet did not overaccept the audited rows.
conclusions.detail: The tracked SME-100 audit found 12 rows with mapped register/scope evidence. Nine were anatomical-extent corrections such as upper arm versus whole upper limb, only three were clear Sino→native shifts, and two instances explicitly permitted coherent all-native or all-Sino alternatives. Sonnet overaccepted 0/12 of these rows. The earlier guide-comparison observation was in-sample and untracked and must not be generalized into a systematic judge blind spot. Re-test on independently reviewed batch 2 before making a population-level claim.

conclusions.statement: SME register feedback should be encoded as category-, anatomical-extent-, and parallelism-aware rules; a single global Sino-Korean→native-Korean direction is not sufficient.
conclusions.detail: In the tracked SME-100 audit, anatomical scope corrections dominated the mapped examples, while true Sino→native preferences were a small subset and spinal feedback allowed either native or Sino terminology provided the coordinated list stayed internally parallel. The practical rule is therefore to distinguish whole limb from limb segment first, preserve category-specific established terminology, and enforce within-term consistency. Directional guide induction remains a hypothesis requiring out-of-sample batch-2 validation.

conclusions.statement: Similarity-only confidence needs complementary error signals, but the current phonetic-echo rule is a conservative candidate generator—not a validated high-recall transliteration detector—and every signal requires independent calibration.
conclusions.detail: The established LLM-judge experiment shows semantic substitutions can be surfaced for review. A new tracked transliteration audit of 24 observed cases (10 labelled errors, 14 benign/translated cases) finds the current 0.70 rule at 80% precision but only 40% recall; an audit-optimal 0.66 reaches 75% precision and 60% recall, with frontier flags rising from 6 to 9. Thus targeted features are preferable to a single similarity gate, but they do not yet 'close' the transliteration gap and must remain triage signals rather than automatic verdicts.

conclusions.statement: Similarity-only confidence needs complementary error signals, but the current phonetic-echo rule is a conservative candidate generator—not a validated high-recall transliteration detector—and every signal requires independent calibration.
conclusions.detail: The established LLM-judge experiment shows semantic substitutions can be surfaced for review. A reproducible tracked transliteration audit using a versioned 24-case observed benchmark (10 labelled errors, 14 benign/translated cases) finds the current 0.70 rule at 80% precision but only 40% recall; an audit-optimal 0.66 reaches 75% precision and 60% recall, with frontier flags rising from 6 to 9. Thus targeted features are preferable to a single similarity gate, but they do not yet close the transliteration gap and must remain triage signals rather than automatic verdicts.

conclusions.statement: SME batch-2 provenance: the 100 terms the SME reviewed (returned 2026-08-09) are the output of run ddbe48e77705 (flow sme-batch2-diverse-gemma-translate, 2026-07-14, diverse selection seed 20260714, fresh gemma4-26b-qat translate) — NOT data/sme_review/2026-07-12/batch2_balanced_100.csv (balanced seed 20260712, pool translations), which shares only 17/100 sctids.
conclusions.detail: Confirmed by exact join against the returned xlsx: 100/100 sctid overlap with the ddbe48e77705 artifact and 99/100 identical translations (the one difference is a spacing variant). The sent CSV is preserved at data/sme_review/2026-07-14/batch2_diverse_sent_100.csv and registered as source sme_batch2_diverse_sent.

conclusions.statement: The batch-2 SME translations reproduce at 86% exact match (chrF 95.2) after full loss and deterministic rebuild of the exemplar vector collection; residual diffs are minor synonym/word-order/spacing flips at temperature 0.
conclusions.detail: The live Qdrant had lost exemplars_pooled_legacy_ko_8d5bcc2e (container remounted to a fresh dir on 2026-08-05 during the Spanish test). Collection rebuilt deterministically from data/EN-KO/all_bilingual_pairs.csv (514,756 points, BGE-M3); reproduction run 778105649302 (flow sme-batch2-repro-translate, gemma4-26b-qat + style guide v5.1, temp 0, exemplars served from the per-collection lookup cache) reproduced the sent file at 86% exact / 95.2 chrF. The 14-15 differing rows show only minor lexical/word-order/spacing drift, consistent with translate-stage code changes merged between 2026-07-14 and 2026-08-06 (unified render/provider, retry/timeout).

conclusions.statement: Style guide v6.0 (hand-encoded SME Q&A rulings) beats v5.1 on the held-out SME gold test split: 23.1% vs 17.9% exact (chrF 61.4 vs 59.4, composite 0.504 vs 0.475), and eliminates contrast hallucinations (2 flagged → 0) — the deterministic encoding banked a real win before any optimisation.
conclusions.detail: 39-term held-out multi-reference split (seed 20260809), gemma4-26b-qat + pooled leak-excluded exemplars, temp 0. v6.0 is now the GEPA seed. Small n — confidence medium; the direction is consistent with the error profile (word-preference dominated).

conclusions.statement: Surface metrics cannot grade the SME acceptability margin: on non-identical pairs (9 acceptable-variation vs 120 partial/wrong), AUC is chance for exact (0.50), chrF (0.51) and BGE-M3 cosine (0.45) — a preferred-synonym swap is indistinguishable from a wrong-preference swap by string or embedding similarity. GEPA's reward must therefore be multi-reference spacing-normalised exact (synonyms as references) plus enforced hard-rule/contrast penalties; cosine partial-credit thresholds would optimise noise.
conclusions.detail: The multi-ref view is trivially separable (AUC 1.0) because every acceptable candidate is itself a reference — identity leakage, not signal. Only 9 informative positives exist, so this is directional; it matches the earlier error-class-detector finding that embeddings miss SME-WRONG cases. A calibrated LLM judge remains the future path to partial credit on the margin.

conclusions.statement: The clean GEPA re-opt (seed v6.0, SME-gold in-domain splits, Opus 5 reflection, hard-rule + contrast penalties) improved dev (0.397→0.498) but did NOT transfer to held-out: 20.5% exact / chrF 55.5 vs v6.0's 23.1% / 61.4 — the promotion gate fails and v6.0 remains the production prompt. This replicates the earlier leak-free finding that the hand style guide beats GEPA, now under the most favourable GEPA setup available.
conclusions.detail: n=39 test so 9-vs-8 exact terms is noise-level, but the chrF gap (61.4→55.5) is consistent across rows and the gate is one-directional. Likely cause: 29-row dev overfit — GEPA's prompt (11.7k chars) compressed away v6.0 detail that matters on unseen terms. Both prompts produce zero contrast-fidelity flags (the penalty + hard rules held). Future GEPA attempts should wait for a larger SME-labelled dev pool (batch-3+) or use cross-validation over the 161 train+dev rows. Artifact preserved at style_guide/style_guide_ko_gepa_sme_gold_v1.md.

conclusions.statement: CORRECTED (supersedes conclusion 27): after fixing the gold data (8/200 batch-1 cells carried unparsed 'or'-alternates, 'preferred term:' prefixes or trailing commas; X-ray rows predate the SME's 단순 촬영 ruling), v5.1 and v6.0 are statistically indistinguishable on the 39-row held-out split — both 17.9% exact like-for-like. v6.0 remains the production prompt on compliance grounds, not exact-match: it deterministically encodes the SME's explicit rulings and holds contrast fidelity at 0 flags (0.16% at 5,012-term production scale vs ~5% under v5.1).
conclusions.detail: The original 23.1% vs 17.9% gap was partly measurement artifact: cleaning the gold moved v6.0's old translations to 28.2%, and re-running under the augmented exemplar pool moved it back to 17.9% while v5.1 stayed at 17.9%. Every pairwise difference is 1-2 terms out of 39 (binomial sigma ~6pts) and the exemplar-pool era flips rankings, so this test set cannot rank prompts at this granularity. Exact-vs-gold remains a lower bound on SME acceptability: of 3 matches 'lost' to exemplar augmentation, 2 were SME-blessed synonym variants (조영/조영술, 하지/다리) the metric cannot credit.

conclusions.statement: CORRECTED (supersedes conclusion 29): under like-for-like corrected conditions the GEPA-optimised guide actually scores highest on the held-out split (23.1% exact / composite 0.512 vs v6.0's 17.9% / 0.496, 0 contrast flags) — the earlier gate rejection reflected dirty gold plus a different exemplar-pool era, not a stable ranking. However the difference is 2 terms out of 39 (within noise), so the honest verdict is: GEPA-v1 is competitive with the hand guides, and a 39-row test cannot decide promotion. Decision: keep v6.0 in production (deterministic ruling compliance), treat the GEPA guide as a live candidate, and settle promotion with SME judgement (e.g. batch-3 A/B) or a materially larger labelled set.
conclusions.detail: Corrected triple (cleaned gold, augmented exemplars, temp 0): GEPA 23.1%/chrF 62.4/composite 0.512; v6.0 17.9%/62.3/0.496; v5.1 17.9%/64.2/0.510 (v5.1 had 1 contrast hallucination; the other two 0). Under the original conditions the ordering was v6.0 > GEPA > v5.1 — ranking instability across an orthogonal condition change is itself evidence the eval lacks power. Reinforces conclusion 28.

conclusions.statement: Translation model choice is the dominant accuracy lever, dwarfing prompt optimisation: on the 200-row SME gold set with the identical v6.0 recipe (cleaned exemplar pool, temp 0), Claude Opus scores 37.5% exact / chrF 72.1, Qwen 3.8-Max 35.0% / 71.1, and gemma4-26b-qat 30.0% / 66.3-67.1 — all with zero contrast-fidelity flags. The +5 to +7.5pt model gaps are 3-5x larger than any prompt-side effect measured tonight.
conclusions.detail: Qwen 3.8-Max added as qwen38-max-remote (DashScope, same endpoint/key as 3.7-Max; DASHSCOPE_API_KEY now provided to the MCP service via systemd EnvironmentFile). Claude Sonnet could not be measured — two attempts hit subscription-window rejections (156/200 errors). Production trade-off to decide: gemma is local/free at 30%, Qwen 3.8-Max is paid API at 35% (200 terms ≈ 11 min at 0.3 req/s), Opus is subscription-throttled (concurrency 2) at 37.5%. Exact-vs-gold remains a lower bound on SME acceptability throughout.

conclusions.statement: GEPA prompt optimisation consistently fails to transfer from dev to held-out on this task: round 2 (seeded from the GEPA-1 guide, cleaned gold, Opus reflection) improved dev to 0.501 but scored 15.4% exact / chrF 59.5 on the held-out 39 — below both GEPA-1 (23.1%) and v6.0 (17.9%). Two rounds, two dev-overfits with a 29-row val set; stop GEPA iterations until the labelled pool grows materially (batch-3+) and spend optimisation effort on model choice and gold/exemplar hygiene instead.
conclusions.detail: Guide artifacts preserved (style_guide_ko_gepa_sme_gold_v1/v2.md). Complementary negative: a judge-guided correction round HURT (31.0%→25.0%, run a9c14eb39e1e) because the gemma acceptability judge over-triggers on acceptable rows. Neutral-positive: exemplar-pool cleaning (39k exact dupes + 5.5k ', NA' EDI artifacts removed — found via the new per-run prompt capture, prompts_<tag>.jsonl) left exact unchanged (30.0%) with chrF +0.8 and fewer contrast flags — kept for hygiene.

conclusions.statement: Qwen 3.8-Max's reasoning mode is pure waste on this task: disabling it (enable_thinking=false) cut the 200-row translate wall-clock from 987.9s to 41.8s (23.6x faster; 2,853 -> 13 output tokens per call) with NO accuracy cost — 35.0% exact both, chrF 71.9 vs 71.1, composite 0.614 vs 0.608, 0 contrast flags both. The 5,012-term production deliverable therefore costs ~18 minutes on Qwen 3.8-Max, not the ~4-5 hours implied by the thinking-on rate.
conclusions.detail: Root cause: the enable_thinking=false switch lives in the model catalogue's per-model llm_params bundle (gemma4-26b-qat has one; both Qwen-Max entries never did — qwen37-max-remote's notes only TOLD a human to set it). Fixed by pinning llm_params on qwen38-max-remote (DashScope accepts top-level enable_thinking and chat_template_kwargs.enable_thinking; both verified). ACTION: qwen37-max-remote still carries the same latent defect. Separately confirmed: DashScope exposes the OpenAI-compatible Batch API (/v1/files upload with purpose=batch + /v1/batches both return 200) for ~50% cost at a 24h window — but at ~18 minutes synchronous for the full pool, batch is not needed at this scale.

conclusions.statement: MEASUREMENT BUG (now fixed): multi-reference scoring was silently inert for every datasource-backed eval. `_eval_set_from_datasource` hard-wired `all_references` to the single target column in BOTH copies of the graph compiler (pipelines/graph.py and the plugin's snomed_translation/graph.py), so `evaluation.multi_ref=true` had no effect and every SME-accepted synonym scored as a miss. With it fixed, Qwen 3.8-Max + v6.0 scores 39.5% exact / chrF 73.7 on the 200-row SME gold (was 35.0% / 71.6); 28 of 200 rows now score against a non-canonical accepted reference. All earlier tonight's numbers were single-reference lower bounds — rankings hold (all models measured identically), absolute levels were understated.
conclusions.detail: Found by checking performance on the SME samples: the same translations scored 70/200 in-run but 79/200 offline against ko_all. Two independent copies of the compiler had to be patched — the app-level fix alone changed nothing because the plugin's copy shadows it for these runs. Gold also gained SME-declared acceptability: 조영상→영상 ruling-updated variants for pre-ruling batch-1 rows (batch-2 gold contains ZERO 조영상, confirming the ruling holds) and the SME's explicit either-form equivalences 조영↔조영술 and 투시 검사↔투시술. Corrected head-to-head: Qwen 3.8-Max 39.5% / chrF 73.7 vs gemma4-26b-qat 33.5% / 68.7 — the +6pt model gap is unchanged in direction and slightly wider.

conclusions.statement: Performance on the SME-reviewed samples is even across batches and shows real recovery on previously-rejected terms: Qwen 3.8-Max + v6.0 scores 39% on batch-1 and 40% on batch-2 (no recency overfit), and on the 120 terms the SME rated Partial/Wrong it now produces the SME's own correction for ~30% while still emitting the exact rejected rendering for only 8%.
conclusions.detail: Breakdown by the SME's original verdict: batch2/CORRECT 57%, batch2/PARTIAL 29%, batch1/ACCEPTABLE 45%, batch1/PARTIAL 33%. The production run itself (6ba05d4eca9a) scores 38.4% on the 177 reviewed concepts inside the active pool vs gemma's 35.6%, consistent with the eval. Leakage check clean: 0/177 reviewed concepts had an SME gold rendering surviving into their shown exemplars (self-exclusion works). Residual 8% repeat-offenders are mostly cases where our output complies with an SME-stated rule but the gold picked the other blessed variant — diminishing returns without new SME input.

conclusions.statement: Exemplar-pool changes must be DECLARATIVE AND TRACKED, not in-place edits. The raw pool is now treated as immutable (regenerable via build_en_ko_pairs.py --combine-only); curation is expressed as versioned rules (configs/ko/pool_rules/ko.yaml, each rule carrying rationale + evidence links) applied by a curate_exemplar_pool node that writes a SEPARATE csv, reports per-rule match counts and the rules content hash as run metrics, and registers as its own source (pooled_curated) so raw-vs-curated is a flow edit rather than a file mutation.
conclusions.detail: Prompted by two undocumented in-place pool mutations made earlier in this session, one of which was actively WRONG: a (en,ko) dedup removed 39,056 rows that the builder keeps ON PURPOSE (its dedup key includes `source`, so the same pair from EDI and SNOMED coexists with distinct provenance shown to the model). Both edits are now reverted — the raw pool is byte-restored to its documented 514,756 rows. v1 rules drop 222 pairs teaching SME-overruled forms (X선/방사선 영상 촬영 for X-ray, 조영상 for images) and append SME gold with post-ruling rewrites applied, fixing self-inflicted contamination (발목 x선 had been retrieved as an exemplar tagged SME_gold_v1). A third rule (EDI bracketed billing qualifiers) is documented but DISABLED: it matches 59% of the pool, so the observed noise is a retrieval-ranking problem, not a content problem.

conclusions.statement: The 200-row SME gold eval has a test-retest noise floor of roughly +/-1-2 points: three byte-identical temp-0 runs scored 75/74/76 of 200 (37.5%/37.0%/38.0%) with 18-25 translations differing and 4-5 exact-match flips between any pair. Any difference below ~3 points on this set is not interpretable, and a 0.04% exemplar-pool change flipped 28 of 200 rows — mostly unrelated register coin-flips (절구/비구, 허리근/요근, 종골/발꿈치븀) — so retrieval perturbation, not just sampling, drives the variance.
conclusions.detail: Consequences for tonight's claims: the curated-vs-raw comparison (35.5% vs 37.5%) is INDISTINGUISHABLE FROM NOISE — curation is retained on correctness grounds (it stops the prompt contradicting our own enforced hard rules) but has NO demonstrated accuracy benefit. The targeted subpopulation (11 X-ray/-gram/-graphy terms) scored 4/11 in both arms. Model-choice gaps (Qwen 3.8-Max vs gemma, ~+6pts) survive this noise floor; style-guide gaps of 4-5pts are marginal and should be re-tested with repeats. Deterministic decoding is NOT reproducible here: vLLM/API batching changes token choices run to run. Future comparisons on this set should report a mean of >=3 repeats, or move to a larger labelled pool.

conclusions.statement: Reasoning/thinking mode is now an explicit per-node switch (translate node `thinking` param) rather than an inherited model-catalogue default, and it is backend-aware: Claude's `thinking` key vs vLLM/DashScope's `enable_thinking` + chat_template_kwargs. The effective state is logged and captured in the run's prompts artifact. This was a genuine measurement defect: Opus had been compared against Qwen while running with thinking ON and Qwen with it OFF.
conclusions.detail: Two bugs found while building it: (1) the graph compiler never forwarded the param at all (a `if params.get(...)` style test would also have silently dropped `false`) so the first 'no-think' run silently ran with thinking ON; (2) setting all conventions at once leaked Claude's `thinking` key into the DashScope payload and 400'd every request. Both fixed; the effective regime is now printed as e.g. `thinking=False (node override)`.

conclusions.statement: Opus's lead does NOT come from its reasoning budget: with thinking explicitly DISABLED it scores 42.0% exact / chrF 74.4, inside the 40.5-43.0 spread of its own thinking-ON runs. Conversely Qwen 3.8-Max gains slightly WITH thinking (40.5% vs 38.0-39.5% without) at 23x the wall-clock. Under one frozen, thinking-matched condition the model gap narrows to roughly 2-3 points (Opus ~42%, Qwen ~39-40.5%) — at the edge of the +/-1-2 point noise floor, and much smaller than the 5-point gap claimed from the unmatched comparison.
conclusions.detail: Frozen condition: patched gold (SME 'original translation can be used as a synonym' alternates recovered), raw pool 8d5bcc2e with NO SME gold in retrieval (no sibling-gold leakage), multi-ref live. Opus thinking-ON 43.0/40.5/42.0 (mean 41.8, spread 2.5pt); Opus thinking-OFF 42.0 (n=1); Qwen thinking-OFF 38.0/39.0/39.5/39.0 (mean 38.9, spread 1.5pt); Qwen thinking-ON 40.5 (n=1, 966s vs 22s). Practical read: thinking buys Qwen ~1.5pt for 40x the time, and buys Opus nothing measurable. Cost/throughput therefore dominates the production choice, since Opus is subscription-throttled at concurrency 2 (~9.5 min per 200 rows vs Qwen's 22s).

conclusions.statement: DeepSeek-V4-Flash added as a model (official DeepSeek API, OpenAI-compatible at https://api.deepseek.com/v1, DEEPSEEK_API_KEY) and benchmarked: 34.0% exact / chrF 69.7 on the 200-row SME gold under the frozen condition — below Qwen 3.8-Max (~39%) and Opus (~42%), and comparable to local gemma4-26b-qat (33.5%). Fast and cheap (200 rows in 16s, 17 output tokens/call) but not competitive on quality for this task.
conclusions.detail: n=1 at a +/-1-2pt noise floor, so treat the gap to Qwen (~5pt) as probable and the gap to gemma (~0.5pt) as unresolved. Frozen condition: v6.0, patched gold, raw pool 8d5bcc2e, multi-ref live, reasoning off.

conclusions.statement: Reasoning-mode control needs a PER-MODEL declared convention, not a shared guess: DeepSeek SILENTLY IGNORES `enable_thinking` (kept emitting 123-180 reasoning tokens with it set to false) and honours only `reasoning_effort: none` / `thinking: {type: disabled}`, while DashScope 400s on Claude's `thinking` key and the Claude Agent SDK accepts only that key. The model catalogue now carries `thinking_style` (sdk | enable_thinking | reasoning_effort) and the translate stage dispatches on it.
conclusions.detail: The silent-ignore failure is the dangerous one: without checking output tokens per call there is no sign the setting did nothing, and a whole benchmark would silently compare a reasoning model against a non-reasoning one. Cheap standing check: output tokens/call in usage.json (~13-17 = reasoning off; 130+ = reasoning on). Verified on the DeepSeek run: 17 tokens/call.
